extracted.intended_audience: courtiers/gentlemen seeking to cultivate tasteful wit and pleasantries at court
extracted.subtask_description: Advice and rules for a courtier on producing laughter and witty pleasantries in courtly company, covering what to say, how to say it, whom to mock, and acceptable forms (stories, short sayings, practical joking).

rubrics_metrics.name: Source of the laughable: incongruity/distortion
rubrics_metrics.description: "the occasion and as it were the source from which the laughable springs, lies in a kind of distortion; for we laugh only at those things that have incongruity in them and that seem amiss without being so."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Laughter arises from things that are incongruous yet not truly amiss; when crafting pleasantries favor situations or descriptions that present a harmless distortion or mismatch. (Implicit anti-pattern: material lacking incongruity will not provoke laughter.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe bounds: do not be a perpetual buffoon
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not seemly for the Courtier to be always making men laugh, nor yet by those means that are made use of by fools or drunken men, by the silly, the nonsensical, and likewise by buffoons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid the techniques of buffoons, parasites, and drunken fools. Do not make constant or crude attempts at humour; moderation and dignity are essential to courtly wit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose targets with discretion (who to deride)
rubrics_metrics.description: We must diligently consider the bounds and limits of exciting laughter by derision, and who it is we deride... not at a poor unfortunate nor an open rascal and blackguard... nor those who are universal favourites and beloved by all and powerful... proper to flout and laugh at the vices of those who are neither so wretched... nor so wicked... nor so great that a touch of their wrath can do much harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not mock the truly wretched (provokes pity) or the dangerously powerful (provokes enmity). Prefer targets whose faults invite ridicule without moral or political risk. Consider social consequences before deriding anyone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Same situations can yield praise or censure
rubrics_metrics.description: From the same occasion whence we draw our laughable witticisms, we may likewise draw serious phrases of praise or censure, and sometimes by using the same words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that wording and situations are versatile: the same material can be framed for praise, satire, or censure. Use framing and tone to guide audience interpretation (example: the lady at mass yielding different remarks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Three kinds of pleasantries (forms of wit)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are three varieties: (1) rendering the effect of a thing by means of urbane and amusing long narrative, (2) the swift and keen readiness of a single phrase, and (3) practical joking, which includes narrative, short sayings, and some action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the form appropriate to occasion and company: extended anecdotes and mimicry, short pointed sallies or puns, or active practical jokes. Each form has different risks and requirements for success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative/storytelling pleasantry: vividness and permissible invention
rubrics_metrics.description: This kind... almost to amount to story-telling... it is allowable for a man to fabricate as much as he pleases, without blame; and in speaking the truth, to adorn it with a little falsity, overstating or understating as the occasion requires.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use gesture and the speaking voice to 'paint' the scene so listeners 'may seem to see' the thing described. Embellishment and small fabrications are permissible to improve effect, provided dignity and plausibility remain. Written compositions can also use this method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mimicry/imitation: covert, clever, and dignified
rubrics_metrics.description: Imitation... cannot be without cleverness; besides governing words and gestures... we must needs be discreet, and pay great heed to the place and time, and to the persons with whom we are speaking, and not descend to buffoonery... give only a fleeting and covert imitation, always preserving the dignity of a gentleman, without uttering foul words or performing acts that are less than seemly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mimic sparingly and subtly: suggest more than you show. Avoid gross facial contortions, obscene language, or full clowning. Consider audience and setting to avoid offense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid excessively biting jibes at physical defects
rubrics_metrics.description: We ought to avoid too stinging jibes, especially at deformities of face or person; for... to employ this method too bitterly is the act not only of a buffoon but of an enemy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical deformities may supply material but should not be used cruelly. Excessive nastiness is dishonorable and alienating, not witty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe minor follies and affectations gracefully
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe gracefully certain defects of others — unimportant ones however and undeserving greater punishment, such as follies, sometimes mere absurdities or sometimes accompanied by a quick and pungent dash of liveliness; likewise certain extreme affectations; sometimes a huge and well-constructed lie.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on trivial or amusing eccentricities rather than serious faults. Use lively, graceful description to turn small absurdities into comic effect (examples: peasants' exaggerated complaints, affectations of nobles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Short sayings: avoid malice and spite
rubrics_metrics.description: In these short sayings the Courtier must take care not to appear malicious and spiteful, and not to utter witticisms and arguzie solely to annoy and cut to the quick; because for the sin of their tongue such men often suffer in all their members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short quips should be clever, not mean-spirited. Malicious sallies risk retaliation and social harm. Keep repartee sharp but not cruel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambiguity and puns as forms of wit
rubrics_metrics.description: Of the ready pleasantries that are contained in a short saying, those are keenest that arise from ambiguity... punning witticisms have much sharpness... play upon the double meaning of the phrase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use double meanings and ambiguity to achieve cleverness; ambiguity often yields admiration for ingenuity even when not uproariously funny. Combine puns with other devices for greater effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unexpectedness (saying the opposite of what is expected)
rubrics_metrics.description: That kind of witticism which is most used to excite laughter, is when we are prepared to hear one thing and the speaker says another, and it is called 'the unexpected.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surprise the audience by defying expectations; unexpected twists in phrasing or content produce strong comic effect—especially when combined with wordplay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Care with puns: avoid flat, forced, or overbiting jests
rubrics_metrics.description: We must be careful and play very lightly with our words, and avoid those that make the sally flat or that seem forced; and also those... that are too biting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure puns feel natural and fresh; forced or predictable wordplay falls flat. Avoid biting jests that wound without provocation (example: mockery of the one-eyed man).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use an adversary's words against him
rubrics_metrics.description: Those have very good grace that are made by taking the very words and sense from another man's taunt and turning them against him and striking him with his own weapons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Skillful retorts that mirror and invert a taunt are highly effective and socially admired. Prepare and deploy quick countering that reframes the insult back upon the speaker.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word-play techniques: adding/omitting letters, repurposing verses, name-interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Playing on words consists in changing a word by either adding or omitting a letter or a syllable... quote a verse or two, applying it to a purpose different from that which the author intends... It is also amusing to interpret names, and to pretend some reason why the man... bears such a name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ varied linguistic tricks—phonetic alterations, misreadings, ironic quotations, and playful etymologies—to craft witty lines. Use these devices to surprise, flatter, or deflate, keeping dignity intact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical joking: include action but with caution
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical joking... in which long narratives and short sayings have place, and also some action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical jokes can be comic but involve physical action and greater risk. Ensure such jokes are appropriate to the company, do not humiliate or harm, and preserve the courtier's decorum.
